messages:
nidhi: Heads-up: customer hit a failover > cross-account decrypt issue with MRKs during a region outage. TL;DR: encrypted DEKs wouldn't decrypt after we routed traffic to a replica region.
samir: ugh. do we have the CloudTrail traces? any errors from KMS returned to the app?
nidhi: yes. app got InvalidCiphertextException from KMS in the replica region. CloudTrail shows kms:Decrypt calls in replica region with AccessDenied for principal arn:aws:sts::222333444:assumed-role/our-crossacct-role
kevin: common gotcha: MRK replicas don't inherit grants. key policies replicate but explicit grants are regional and tied to the key ARN. if we relied on grants generated in primary, they won't exist on replica.
samir: right. did the customer use grants for cross-account decrypt or a key policy that allows the other account/role?
nidhi: they used grants (short-lived) from a provisioning job in primary. we pushed ciphertext to S3 (replicated), then routed reads to replica region; the DEKs were encrypted under the MRK in primary RPC, but decrypt attempted against local replica CMK expecting the same grant.
security-oncall: quick checklist: 1) CloudTrail event ids for kms:Decrypt 2) confirm which CMK ID was used (Replica vs Primary) 3) check for GrantCreated events. That'll show mismatch.
kevin: mitigation options we've used: - avoid cross-account grants for MRK workflows; use key-policy cross-account principal(s) instead (so all replicas accept the principal). - or proactively duplicate grants on each replica via automation when created. - or on failover, call the primary region KMS decrypt (if network/latency/policy allows) to rewrap DEK and return local ciphertext.
nidhi: can we add the recommended pattern to runbook? customer asked about end-to-end suggestions: they prefer not to call primary region for decrypt during outage.
samir: suggested runbook patch: prefer key-policy allowlist for trusted account roles so replicas accept decrypt; for ephemeral per-host grants, sync grants to replicas with a small lambda that listens to GrantCreated and GrantRevoked CloudWatch events and replicates semantics to replicas (note: you'll need to create new grants in each replica account/region).
kevin: important caveat: IAM principal-based access (via key policy) is better for cross-account reliability, but it broadens blast radius if service role compromised. keep minimal principals and monitor CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt spikes.
security-oncall: audit logging: add a dedicated CloudTrail trail for kms events, enable log-forwarding to our SIEM, and add an alert for "kms:Decrypt AccessDenied" patterns during a region failover window.
devops-bot: deploy-note from pipeline: added a starter terraform module snippet to update MRK replica key policies and a lambda scaffold for grant sync (PR: #4021).
nidhi: thanks team. I'll draft runbook edits: include (1) explanation of grant vs policy behavior for MRKs, (2) step-by-step mitigation options (policy change, grant-sync tool, primary-decrypt fallback), (3) audit checks and SIEM alerts. tagging @kevin for a short write-up on risk tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
